title: improv·artist · monumental (Anish Kapoor)
mutation_directive: improv artist: monumental via Anish Kapoor

improv_extras.practice: void, mirror, blood-red pigment, scale; the form opens onto absence

v1.feedback: Strong concept-to-code: differential growth on a concave paraboloid with an empty void center is a legit Kapoor 'Descent into Limbo' translation, and the bone→rust→abyss palette is exactly the restrained earth-tone register this gallery wants. The breathing displacement (0.003 amplitude) is tastefully minimal. Two refinements: the camera at (3,16,18) looking down at (0,-3,0) is quite steep — pulling back to a shallower polar angle (say maxPolarAngle ~0.62) would let the rim's differential-growth silhouette read as monumental rather than cartographic; and the additive blending on 50k particles risks washing out the bowl's interior darkness at the rim edge — consider normal blending with a pre-multiplied alpha falloff so the void truly swallows light rather than accumulating glow.

v2.feedback: Strong concept — Kapoor's Descent into Limbo as differential-growth bowl crater is a direct hit on void/absence, and the architecture is sound (spatial-hash growth, DataTexture upload, custom blending to keep the void truly dark, manual fog uniforms avoiding the auto-inject pitfall). However, the vertex shader is truncated so the full color palette and particle distribution logic can't be verified — if the fragment shader uses oversaturated blood-reds at high saturation to reference Kapoor's pigment work, that would violate the palette constraint; keep any red in the rust/dried-blood range (HSL sat <50%). The 50K particle count with only 4K growth vertices risks the rim reading as a diffuse cloud rather than a crisp coral edge — consider concentrating more particles tightly on the growth curve with a steeper falloff, or rendering the growth ring as a secondary LineLoop geometry underneath the particle scatter to anchor the silhouette. Finally, ensure the bowl occupies >30% of the default viewport — with camera at (0, 3.5, 18) and FOV 42, the form may sit small; pulling the camera to z≈12 or widening FOV to 50 would help it feel monumental.
